title: Yutou World
subtitle: Start with favorite stories, then explore life, the body, Earth, space, energy, and human-made systems.

positioning.animationWorldDecision: Animation World is the interest gateway on the homepage. Visually it is World 0, but it is not counted as one of the six knowledge worlds.
positioning.reason: Animation themes help attract the child into learning, while the knowledge system stays stable. Animation World carries entry, review, and transfer practice.
positioning.homeLearningPromise: Each board lights up one way to understand the world: observe, classify, compare, explain, and express.

homeHero.title: Yutou World
homeHero.subtitle: Start from stories, then light up real-world knowledge.
homeHero.childIntro: Do you want to visit the story world first, or see how bodies, animals, Earth, and space work?
homeHero.parentIntro: This is not a children’s encyclopedia page. It uses a consistent visual structure to build classification, mechanism thinking, comparison, and expression.

sections.title: Interest Gateway
sections.description: Stories and characters children love help bring attention to observation, tasks, relationships, and expression.

sections.title: Six Knowledge Worlds
sections.description: A stable knowledge map that connects scattered interests into systematic understanding.

worlds.name: Animation World
worlds.childOneLiner: Start with favorite heroes and teams, then learn to notice stories, missions, and character relationships.
worlds.parentNote: Animation World is not a knowledge category by itself. It is an interest gateway that turns familiar stories into practice in observation, classification, teamwork, value judgment, and expression.

entryCard.title: Start with favorite stories
entryCard.subtitle: Spider heroes, Paw Patrol, and more story boards.

topicCards.title: Spider Universe Visual Storyboard
topicCards.cardDescription: See how different spider heroes face growth, responsibility, choices, and teamwork.
topicCards.childDescription: Every spider hero has a challenge, and every hero has a brave way to try.
topicCards.suggestedRoute: Character cards → world relationships → growth mission → tell the story myself

topicCards.title: Paw Patrol Mission Command Center
topicCards.cardDescription: Use missions, tools, and roles to understand teamwork.
topicCards.childDescription: Each pup has a special skill, and the team solves problems together.
topicCards.suggestedRoute: Mission map → team roles → tools → badge challenge

worlds.name: Life World
worlds.childOneLiner: Meet animals, plants, and insects, and see how living things grow, eat, and protect themselves.
worlds.parentNote: Life World first trains classification and ecological relationship thinking, then expands from common animals, insects, and plants into food chains, ecosystems, and evolution.

entryCard.title: Life World
entryCard.subtitle: Animals, plants, insects, and ecological relationships.

topicCards.title: Animal Classification Tree
topicCards.cardDescription: Put animals back into the right big groups.

topicCards.title: Insects and Spiders Detective Station
topicCards.cardDescription: Use leg count, antennae, and body structure to spot differences.

topicCards.title: Dinosaur and Fossil Detective Station
topicCards.cardDescription: Use fossil clues to infer what dinosaurs looked like and how they lived.

topicCards.title: Forest Pond Ecosystem Web
topicCards.cardDescription: See how sunlight, water, plants, animals, and decomposers form a web.

topicCards.title: A Plant’s Life
topicCards.cardDescription: From seed to flower and fruit.

worlds.name: Body World
worlds.childOneLiner: Go inside the body and see how blood, the heart, bones, and the brain work together.
worlds.parentNote: Body World explains internal body mechanisms through friendly visuals, avoiding scary or bloody imagery while building understanding of roles, health habits, and basic physiology.

entryCard.title: Body World
entryCard.subtitle: Tiny work teams inside the body.

topicCards.title: Blood Cells 3D
topicCards.cardDescription: Meet red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and plasma.

topicCards.title: Food Travel Team
topicCards.cardDescription: Follow food from the mouth and see how it becomes energy the body can use.

worlds.name: Earth World
worlds.childOneLiner: See why cities, climates, mountains, rivers, oceans, and weather are different around Earth.
worlds.parentNote: Earth World connects real maps, climate zones, natural processes, and daily life, helping children build spatial awareness, environmental differences, and geography basics.

entryCard.title: Earth World
entryCard.subtitle: Cities, climate, maps, and natural forces.

topicCards.title: Globe, Climate Zones, and Cities
topicCards.cardDescription: Why are some places hot and some places cold?

topicCards.title: Water Cycle Travel Station
topicCards.cardDescription: Follow a water drop through evaporation, clouds, rain, rivers, and oceans.

worlds.name: Space World
worlds.childOneLiner: Start with the solar system and see where Earth lives in space.
worlds.parentNote: Space World builds scale, orbit, position relationships, and celestial classification, starting with the solar system, Moon phases, and planet comparison.

entryCard.title: Space World
entryCard.subtitle: The Sun, planets, the Moon, and asteroids.

topicCards.title: Solar System Overview
topicCards.cardDescription: The Sun is in the center, and planets travel around it.

topicCards.title: Moon Phase Observation Station
topicCards.cardDescription: Observe the Moon over time and learn why its shape appears to change.

worlds.name: Matter and Energy World
worlds.childOneLiner: See how water, light, electricity, heat, and energy change.
worlds.parentNote: This world uses observable phenomena as the entry point for basic physics and energy conversion, then later expands into electromagnetism, power generation, fission, and fusion.

entryCard.title: Matter and Energy World
entryCard.subtitle: Light, electricity, heat, water, and energy changes.

topicCards.title: Light and Color
topicCards.cardDescription: Why does a rainbow have many colors?

topicCards.title: Fission and Fusion for Kids
topicCards.cardDescription: Big blocks split apart, small blocks join together, and energy can be released.

worlds.name: Human-Made Systems World
worlds.childOneLiner: See how robots, cities, the internet, and AI systems made by people work.
worlds.parentNote: Human-Made Systems World turns technology and social systems into child-friendly ideas: input, processing, output, feedback, and rules instead of adult engineering details.

entryCard.title: Human-Made Systems World
entryCard.subtitle: Robots, traffic, the internet, and AI.

topicCards.title: Large Language Models for Kids
topicCards.cardDescription: Why can AI answer questions? Can it also make mistakes?

topicCards.title: Robot Workshop
topicCards.cardDescription: Connect sensors, programs, and moving parts to understand how robots work.
